newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss study whether to recall envoy from Iran.
newsitem.headline: Swiss study whether to recall envoy from Iran.

text.p: Neutral Switzerland is studying whether to keep its ambassador in Iran after a German court ruled that Tehran ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish activists, the Foreign Department (ministry) said on Friday.

Germany and Sweden recalled their ambassadors from Iran after the ruling on Thursday and the EU invited other members to join the action. Australia has also ordered its envoy home and Britain said it would do so shortly.
"Before Switzerland takes it own steps, the Foreign Department will now review the situation and make the corresponding proposals to the Federal Council (cabinet)," a spokesman said.
Switzerland has also represented U.S. diplomatic interests in Iran since the U.S. embassy in Tehran was seized by Iranian students in 1980.

Separately, Switzerland's Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Vorort) said it did not expect Swiss exporters to jump at the chance of filling in for Western rivals whose countries distance themselves from Iran due to the Berlin ruling.
